body.translated_text: ...hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of treasures appear from the earth. While he was practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, that many immeasurable, innumerable hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of beings were established in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, the limit of which is not easy to grasp by word or deed; that many immeasurable, innumerable Blessed Buddhas were honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped, and were provided with robes, alms-food, lodging, seats, medicinal requisites for the sick, all pleasant comforts, and delightful dwellings; as many beings were established in the families of merchants, householders, ministers, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, brahmins, and great householders, their limit is not easy to grasp by verbal enumeration; likewise, they were established as rulers of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, as universal monarchs, as world protectors, as <s>Śakras</s>, as <s>Suyāmas</s>, as <s>Saṃtuṣitas</s>, as <s>Sunirmitas</s>, as <s>Vaśavartins</s>, as kings of gods, and as <s>Mahābrahmās</s>; that many immeasurable, innumerable Blessed Buddhas were honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped, and were requested to turn the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>, and their limit is not easy to grasp by verbal enumeration. Having accumulated such merit, while he was practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct for immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, unreckonable, and inexpressible hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, a fragrant, divine, and transcendent scent of sandalwood emanated from his mouth; from all the pores of his skin, the scent of blue lotus emanated; he was the most handsome in all the worlds, graceful, beautiful to behold, endowed with the fullness of a supremely pure and excellent complexion. From his body, adorned with the major and minor marks, manifestations of all jeweled ornaments, manifestations of all garments and robes, manifestations of all flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags, and manifestations of all kinds of music and song issued forth from all the pores of his skin and from the palms of his hands. Manifestations of all kinds of food and drink—solid, soft, to be licked, and liquids—and manifestations of all things for use and enjoyment flowed forth and appeared from the palms of his hands. Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, that monk <s>Dharmākara</s>, having attained the perfection of mastery over all requisites, was, while formerly practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct. When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "But, O Blessed One, has that <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmākara</s>, having awakened to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, passed away into final <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, or has he not yet awakened, or has he awakened in the present, and does he now exist, live, and maintain himself, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>?" The Blessed One said: "That <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has not passed away, nor is he yet to come. Rather, that <s>Tathāgata</s>, having awakened to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, now exists, lives, and maintains himself, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. In the western direction, a hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddha-fields from here, in the world-realm named <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Amitābha</s>, surrounded and honored by immeasurable <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, attended by countless <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and endowed with the infinite perfection of a Buddha-field. And his light is immeasurable, the extent or limit of which is not easy to grasp, as to how many Buddha-fields, how many hundreds of Buddha-fields, how many thousands of Buddha-fields, how many hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields, how many <s>koṭis</s> of Buddha-fields, how many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of Buddha-fields, how many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of Buddha-fields, how many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of Buddha-fields, how many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddha-fields it pervades and remains. Indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>, to be brief, in the eastern direction, hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddha-fields, equal to the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, are constantly pervaded by the light of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>. Likewise, in the southern, western, and northern directions, below, above, and in the intermediate directions, in each single direction all around, hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddha-fields, equal to the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, are constantly pervaded by the light of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, with the exception of those Blessed Buddhas who, by the power of their previous vows, remain pervading the world with a light of the sky, a light of one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, or forty <s>yojanas</s>, a light of a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, a light of a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, a light of a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, up to a light of many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>yojanas</s>. There is no comparison, <s>Ānanda</s>, by which it is possible to grasp the measure of the light of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>. For this reason, <s>Ānanda</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitābha</s> (Immeasurable Light); he is also called <s>Amitaprabha</s> (Immeasurable Splendor), <s>Amitaprabhāsa</s> (Immeasurable Radiance), <s>Asamāptaprabha</s> (Unceasing Light), <s>Asaṅgaprabha</s> (Unattached Light), <s>Apratihataprabha</s> (Unimpeded Light), <s>Nityotsṛṣṭaprabha</s> (Constantly Emitted Light), <s>Divyamaṇiprabha</s> (Divine Jewel Light), <s>Apratihataraśmirājaprabha</s> (Light of the Unimpeded King of Rays), <s>Rañjanīyaprabha</s> (Delightful Light), <s>Premaṇīyaprabha</s> (Lovable Light), <s>Prāmodanīyaprabha</s> (Joyful Light), <s>Prahlādanīyaprabha</s> (Refreshing Light), <s>Ullokanīyaprabha</s> (Light Worthy of Being Seen), <s>Nibandhanīyaprabha</s> (Captivating Light), <s>Acintyaprabha</s> (Inconceivable Light), <s>Atulyaprabha</s> (Incomparable Light), <s>Abhibhūyanarendrāsurendraprabha</s> (Light that Surpasses Kings of Men and Asuras), <s>Abhibhūyacandrasūryajihmīkaraṇaprabha</s> (Light that Surpasses and Eclipses the Moon and Sun), <s>Abhibhūyalokapālaśakrabrahmaśuddhāvāsamaheśvarasarvadevajihmīkaraṇaprabha</s> (Light that Surpasses and Eclipses the World Protectors, Śakra, Brahmā, the Pure Abodes, Maheśvara, and all the gods), and he is called <s>Sarvaprabhāpāragata</s> (One Who Has Gone Beyond All Light). And that light of his is pure, vast, producing bodily comfort, causing mental elation, bringing pleasure, joy, and happiness to gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, humans, and non-humans, and causing joy in the wholesome intentions and the nimble, swift, and discerning intelligence of those in other infinite and boundless Buddha-fields as well. And for this reason, <s>Ānanda</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> could speak for a full <s>kalpa</s>, taking up the name and deeds of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> and beginning with his light, and still not be able to reach the limit of the qualities of that light. Nor would the <s>Tathāgata's</s> confidence be exhausted. For what reason? Because both of these, <s>Ānanda</s>, are immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, and boundless: namely, the splendor of the qualities of the light of that Blessed One, and the unexcelled wisdom and eloquence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> is immeasurable, and it is not easy to grasp its number; as to how many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, how many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, how many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, how many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, how many <s>kaṅkaras</s>, how many <s>biṃbaras</s>, how many <s>niyutas</s>, how many <s>ayutas</s>, how many <s>akṣobhyas</s>, how many <s>vivāhas</s>, how many <s>śrotas</s>, how many <s>jāyas</s>, how many immeasurables, how many innumerables, how many uncountables, how many incomparables, how many inconceivables there are. Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, who has attained mastery of supernatural powers, if he wished, could count all the stars in a three-thousand-great-thousand-fold world system in a single day and night; and if there were a hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of such beings with supernatural powers, and they were to count the first assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> for a hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of years, doing nothing else, by their counting not even a hundredth part would be counted; not a thousandth part, not a hundred-thousandth part, not even a fraction, a comparison, or a semblance would be counted. Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, from the great ocean, eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> deep and immeasurable in breadth, some person were to lift up a single drop of water with the tip of a hair split a hundred times; what do you think, <s>Ānanda</s>, which is greater: the one drop of water lifted up by the tip of a hair split a hundred times, or the mass of water remaining in the great ocean?" He said: "Even a thousand <s>yojanas</s> of the great ocean, O Blessed One, would be small. How much more so the single drop of water lifted up by the tip of a hair split a hundred times." The Blessed One said: "Like that single drop of water is the number of that first assembly that would be counted by those monks like <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, counting for that hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of years; like the mass of water remaining in the great ocean, so should the uncounted portion be seen. What then is to be said of the second, third, and subsequent assemblies of <s>Śrāvakas</s>? Thus, the assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> of that Blessed One is infinite and boundless, and is designated simply as 'immeasurable and innumerable'. And immeasurable, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the lifespan of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, the measure of which is not easy to grasp; as to whether it is so many <s>kalpas</s>, or so many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, or so many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, or so many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, or so many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, or so many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, or so many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, or so many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, or so many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. Rather, <s>Ānanda</s>, the lifespan of that Blessed One is simply immeasurable, boundless. For that reason, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitāyus</s> (Immeasurable Life). And, <s>Ānanda</s>, according to the counting of <s>kalpas</s>, the calculation of <s>kalpas</s>, the conventional designation in this world-realm, it is now ten <s>kalpas</s> since that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, arose and awakened to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the world-realm of that Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s> is named <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss); it is prosperous, flourishing, secure, with abundant food, delightful, and filled with many gods and humans. In that world-realm, <s>Ānanda</s>, there are no hells, no animal births, no realm of hungry ghosts, no bodies of <s>asuras</s>, and no unfortunate births; nor do those jewels that are found in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s> circulate in this world. That world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is stirred by various fragrant breezes, is rich with various flowers and fruits, is adorned with jewel trees, and is frequented by flocks of various birds with pleasing voices, created by the manifestation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And those jewel trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, are of various colors, of many colors, of many hundreds of thousands of colors. There are jewel trees of a golden color, made of gold; there are those of a silver color, made of silver; there are those of a lapis lazuli color, made of lapis lazuli; there are those of a crystal color, made of crystal; there are those of a musāragalva color, made of musāragalva; there are those of a red pearl color, made of red pearls; there are those of an emerald color, made of emerald. There are some jewel trees of two jewels, gold and silver. There are those of three jewels: gold, silver, and lapis lazuli. There are those of four: gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal. There are those of five: gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, and musāragalva. There are those of six: gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, musāragalva, and red pearls. And there are those of seven jewels: gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, musāragalva, red pearls, and the seventh, emerald. There, <s>Ānanda</s>, for the golden trees, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, and flowers are made of gold, and the fruits are made of silver; for the silver trees, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, and flowers are made of silver, and the fruits are made of lapis lazuli; for the lapis lazuli trees, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, and flowers are made of lapis lazuli, and the fruits are made of crystal; for the crystal trees, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, and flowers are made of crystal, and the fruits are made of musāragalva; for the musāragalva trees, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, and flowers are made of musāragalva, and the fruits are made of red pearls; for the red pearl trees, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, and flowers are made of red pearls, and the fruits are made of emerald; for the emerald trees, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, and flowers are made of emerald, and the fruits are made of gold. For some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of gold, the trunks of silver, the main boughs of lapis lazuli, the branches of crystal, the leaves of musāragalva, the flowers of red pearls, and the fruits of emerald; for some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of silver, the trunks of lapis lazuli, the main boughs of crystal, the branches of musāragalva, the leaves of red pearls, the flowers of emerald, and the fruits of gold; for some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of lapis lazuli, the trunks of crystal, the main boughs of musāragalva, the branches of red pearls, the leaves of emerald, the flowers of gold, and the fruits of silver; for some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of crystal, the main boughs of musāragalva, the trunks of red pearls, the branches of emerald, the leaves of gold, the flowers of silver, and the fruits of lapis lazuli; for some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of musāragalva, the trunks of red pearls, the main boughs of emerald, the branches of gold, the leaves of silver, the flowers of lapis lazuli, and the fruits of crystal; for some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of red pearls, the trunks of emerald, the main boughs of gold, the branches of silver, the leaves of lapis lazuli, the flowers of crystal, and the fruits of musāragalva; for some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of emerald, the trunks of gold, the main boughs of silver, the branches of lapis lazuli, the leaves of crystal, the flowers of musāragalva, and the fruits of red pearls; and for some trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots are made of the seven jewels, the trunks are made of the seven jewels, the main boughs are made of the seven jewels, the branches are made of the seven jewels, the leaves are made of the seven jewels, the flowers are made of the seven jewels, and the fruits are made of the seven jewels. And for all those trees, <s>Ānanda</s>, the roots, trunks, main boughs, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are soft, pleasant to the touch, and fragrant; and when stirred by the wind, a lovely and pleasing sound issues from them, which is delightful and not disagreeable to hear. With such trees made of the seven jewels, <s>Ānanda</s>, that Buddha-field is filled, and all around it is enclosed by plantain trunks made of the seven jewels and rows of jewel-palm trees, and everywhere it is covered with golden nets, and all around it is covered with lotuses made of the seven jewels. There are lotuses there half a <s>yojana</s> in size, there are those a <s>yojana</s> in size, there are those two, three, four, or five <s>yojanas</s> in size, and there are those up to ten <s>yojanas</s> in size. And from each jewel lotus, thirty-six thousand <s>koṭis</s> of rays issue forth. And from the tip of each ray, thirty-six thousand <s>koṭis</s> of Buddhas issue forth, with golden-colored bodies, possessing the thirty-two marks of a great person, who, going to immeasurable and innumerable world-realms in the eastern direction, teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Likewise, in the southern, western, and northern directions, below, above, and in the intermediate directions, in the unobstructed world, going to immeasurable and innumerable world-realms, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that Buddha-field, there are no black mountains at all; everywhere there are jewel mountains. There are no Mount <s>Sumerus</s>, kings of mountains, at all; there are no <s>Cakravāḍa</s> or <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s> mountains, kings of mountains, at all; and there are no great oceans. And all around, that Buddha-field is level, delightful, like the palm of the hand, its ground composed of various kinds of jewels. When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "But where, O Blessed One, are those gods of the Four Great Kings who dwell on the slopes of <s>Sumeru</s>, or the Thirty-three gods who dwell on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, established?" The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s>? Where are those who are above this Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains—the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Mahābrahman</s> gods, up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods—where are they established?" He said: "Inconceivable, O Blessed One, is the ripening of actions, the formation of <s>karma</s>." The Blessed One said: "You have understood here, <s>Ānanda</s>, the inconceivable ripening of actions, the formation of <s>karma</s>; but not so inconceivable is the spiritual power of the Blessed Buddhas. And for beings who have performed meritorious deeds and planted roots of merit, the splendor of their merit there is inconceivable." He said: "I have no doubt, uncertainty, or perplexity about this, O Blessed One. Rather, I ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> this question in order to dispel the doubt, uncertainty, and perplexity of future beings." The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, <s>Ānanda</s>; thus should you act. In that world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, rivers of various kinds flow. There are great rivers a <s>yojana</s> in width. There are those up to twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, up to a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in width, and twelve <s>yojanas</s> deep; and all the rivers flow gently, carrying water with various fragrant scents, carrying masses of flowers stirred with various jewels, and have various sweet-sounding murmurs. And from them, <s>Ānanda</s>, issues a pleasing sound as lovely as that of a divine musical instrument with a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of parts, played skillfully in concert. The sound that issues from those great rivers is deep, authoritative, intelligible, clear, pleasant to the ear, captivating to the heart, lovable, charming and pleasing, delightful, not disagreeable, worth hearing, and pleasant to hear as 'inconceivable, peaceful, non-self,' which comes within the range of the sense of hearing of those beings. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, on both banks of those great rivers are rows of various fragrant trees, from which hang various branches, leaves, and clusters of flowers. There, for those beings on the riverbanks who wish to experience divine, non-sensual pleasure and sport, when they descend into the rivers, the water stands ankle-deep for those who wish it so; for those who wish it, it stands knee-deep, waist-deep, armpit-deep, or for those who wish it, neck-deep; and divine pleasures arise. There, for those beings who wish, 'May the water be cool,' for them it becomes cool; for those who wish, 'May it be warm,' for them it becomes warm; for those who wish, 'May it be cool and warm,' for them that water becomes cool and warm, according to their pleasure. And those great rivers flow, filled with water perfumed with the excellent scents of divine tamāla leaves, agaru, kālānusāri, tagara, uragasāra, and sandalwood; covered with divine flowers such as blue lotuses, lotuses, white water lilies, white lotuses, and fragrant flowers; with banks frequented by flocks of birds with pleasing voices, created by the manifestation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, such as swans, cranes, ruddy geese, ducks, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, kuṇālas, kalaviṅkas, and peacocks; adorned with mineral powders, with excellent fords, free from mud, and strewn with golden sand. There, when those beings wish, 'May such intentions of ours be fulfilled,' then precisely such righteous intentions of theirs are fulfilled. And that sound of the water, <s>Ānanda</s>, is so pleasing that it makes the entire Buddha-field known. There, for those beings standing on the riverbanks who wish, 'May this sound not come within the range of our sense of hearing,' it does not come within the range of even their divine sense of hearing. And whoever wishes to hear a certain kind of sound, hears precisely that kind of pleasing sound; for example, the sound of 'Buddha', the sound of '<s>Dharma</s>', the sound of '<s>Saṃgha</s>', the sound of '<s>pāramitā</s> (perfection)', the sound of '<s>bhūmi</s> (stage)', the sound of '<s>bala</s> (power)', the sound of '<s>vaiśāradya</s> (confidence)', the sound of '<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s> (unique qualities of a Buddha)', the sound of '<s>abhijñā</s> (super-knowledge)', the sound of '<s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge)', the sound of 'emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-fabrication, non-arising, non-production, non-existence, cessation', the sound of 'peaceful, utterly peaceful, quiescent', the sound of 'great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity', and the sound of 'attaining the stage of consecration through acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena'. And hearing such sounds, they obtain sublime pleasure and joy, accompanied by seclusion, accompanied by dispassion, accompanied by peace, accompanied by cessation, accompanied by the <s>Dharma</s>, and accompanied by the roots of merit for the complete attainment of enlightenment. And in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is no sound of what is unwholesome at all; there is no sound of hindrances at all; there is no sound of unfortunate states, bad destinies, or downfall at all; there is no sound of suffering at all; even the sound of the feeling that is neither suffering nor pleasure does not exist there, <s>Ānanda</s>; how then could there be suffering or the sound of suffering? For this reason, <s>Ānanda</s>, that world-realm is called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss) in brief, but not in full. Even a <s>kalpa</s> would come to an end while enumerating the causes of happiness in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; but it is not possible to reach the limit of those causes of happiness. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, those beings who have been reborn or will be reborn are all endowed with such complexion, strength, vigor, height and breadth, sovereignty, accumulation of merit, super-knowledges, enjoyment of robes, ornaments, parks, palaces, and pavilions, enjoyment of such sounds, smells, tastes, and touches, and with all such things for use and enjoyment; just like the gods of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> heaven. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, beings do not consume coarse, morsel-by-morsel food. Rather, whatever kind of food they wish for, they perceive that very kind as having been eaten. Their bodies are satisfied, and their limbs are nourished. They do not have to put anything further into their bodies. Their bodies being satisfied, whatever kinds of fragrances they wish for, with precisely such divine fragrances the entire Buddha-field is perfumed. There, for one who does not wish to smell that fragrance, no perception or trace of fragrance arises at all. Likewise, whatever kinds of perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and musical instruments they wish for, with precisely such things the entire Buddha-field is filled. Whatever kind of robes they wish for, of various colors, of many hundreds of thousands of colors, with precisely such jewel-robes the entire Buddha-field is filled; and they perceive themselves as being clothed. Whatever kind of ornaments they wish for, for example: head ornaments, ear ornaments, or ornaments for the neck, hands, and feet, namely: crowns, earrings, bracelets, armlets, chest ornaments, necklaces, ear pendants, rings, golden threads, girdles, golden nets, and nets of all-jewel bangles—they see that Buddha-field filled with such ornaments, inlaid with many hundreds of thousands of jewels. That is: they perceive themselves as adorned with those ornaments from the ornament-trees and with garments. Whatever kind of palace they wish for, of whatever color, form, and shape, of whatever height and breadth, adorned with hundreds of thousands of pinnacles made of various jewels, strewn with various divine fabrics, with jewel couches set with variegated cushions—precisely such a palace appears before them. In those palaces created from their minds, they dwell, play, delight, and enjoy themselves, surrounded and honored by seven thousand <s>apsarases</s>. And in that world-realm, there is no distinction between gods and humans, except that by way of conventional designation they are counted as 'gods' and 'humans'. Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, before a universal monarch, an inferior human, a human eunuch, does not shine, does not glow, does not radiate, is not confident, is not brilliant, in the very same way, before the gods of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> heaven, <s>Śakra</s>, the king of the gods, does not shine, does not glow, does not radiate, that is: with respect to parks, palaces, robes, and ornaments, or sovereignty, or supernatural power, or miraculous displays, or lordship; but not, however, with respect to the realization of the <s>Dharma</s> or the enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s>. There, <s>Ānanda</s>, just as are the gods of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> heaven, so should the humans in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s> be seen. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, when the time of morning has arrived, from all four directions winds blow, whirling and swirling, by which the jewel trees—variegated, beautiful to behold, of various colors, of many colors, perfumed with various fragrant and divine scents—are shaken, thoroughly shaken, stirred, and set in motion;

And with those flowers, that Buddha-field all around becomes a well-formed shape, seven persons deep. Just as some skilled person might spread a carpet of flowers on the ground, arranging it evenly with both hands, variegated and beautiful to behold, in the same way, that Buddha-field becomes covered all around, seven persons deep, with those flowers of various scents and colors. And those kinds of flowers are soft, pleasant to the touch like <s>kācalindika</s> cloth; by way of comparison, when a foot is placed on them, they sink down just four fingers, and when the foot is lifted, they rise up just four fingers. When the morning time has passed, those flowers disappear without a trace. Then that Buddha-field becomes secluded, delightful, and beautiful, not sullied by those previous flowers. Then again

api samantāc caturdiśaṃ vāyavo vānti, ye pūrvavad abhinavāni
puṣpāṇy abhiprakiranti. yathā pūrvāhna eva madhyāhne,
P40
'parāhne kālasamaye, saṃdhyāyāṃ, rātryāḥ prathame
yāme, madhyame paścime ca yāme. taiś ca vātair vāyadbhir
nānāgandhaparivāsitais te sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ santa, evaṃ
sukhasamarpitā bhavanti sma, tad yathāpi nāma nirodhasamāpanno
bhikṣuḥ.
  tasmiṃś cānanda buddhakṣetre sarvaśo 'gnicandrasūrya-
grahanakṣatratārārūpānāṃ tamo'ndhakārasya ca nāmadheya-
prajñaptir api nāsti. sarvaśo rātridivaprajñaptir api
nāsty, anyatra tathāgatavyavahārāt. sarvaśaś cāgāraparigraha-
saṃjñā nāsti.
  tasyāṃ khalu punar ānanda sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau
kāle divyagandhodakameghā abhipravarṣanti. divyāni sarva-
varṇikāni kusumāni, divyāni saptaratnāni, divyaṃ candana-
cūrṇaṃ, divyāś cchatradhvajapatākā abhipravarṣanti. divyāni
vimānāni, divyāni vitānāni dhriyante, divyāni ratnacchatrāṇi
sacāmarāṇy ākāśe dhriyante. divyāni vādyāni pravādyante.
divyāś cāpsaraso nṛtyanti sma.
  tasmin khalu punar ānanda buddhakṣetre ye sattvā
upapannā utpadyanta upapatsyante, sarve te niyatāḥ samyaktve
yāvan nirvāṇāt. tat kasya hetoḥ. nāsti tatra dvayo
rāśyor vyavasthānaṃ prajñaptir vā, yad idam : aniyatyasya
vā mithyātvaniyatasya vā. tad anenāpy ānanda paryāyeṇa
sā lokadhātuḥ sukhāvatīty ucyate saṃkṣiptena, na vistareṇa.
kalpo 'py ānanda parikṣayet, sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau
sukhakāraṇeṣu parikīrtayamāneṣu ; na ca teṣāṃ sukhakāraṇānāṃ
P41
śakyaṃ paryanto 'dhigantum.
  atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyām imā gāthā
abhāṣata :
  sarve pi sattvāḥ sugatā bhaveyuḥ,
  viśuddhajñānāḥ paramārthakovidā.
  te kalpakoṭīm atha vāpi uttarim,
  sukhāvatīvarṇa prakāśayeyuḥ.(1)
  kṣaye kalpakoṭīya vrajeyu tāś ca,
  sukhāvatīye na ca varṇa antaḥ.
  kṣayaṃ na gacchet pratibhā teṣāṃ
  prakāśayantāna tha varṇamālā.(2)
  ye lokadhātūṃ paramāṇusadṛśāṃ
  cchindeya bhindeya rajāṃś ca kuryāt,
  ato bahū uttari lokadhātū
  pūretva dānaṃ ratanehi dadyāt.(3)
  na tā kalāṃ pi upamā pi tasya
  puṇyasya bhontī pṛthulokadhātavaḥ,
  yal lokadhātūya sukhāvatīye
  śrutvaiva nāma bhavatīha puṇyaṃ (4)
  tato bahū puṇya bhaveta teṣāṃ,
  ye śraddhaṇeya jinavacanasaṃjñā.
  śraddhā hi mūlaṃ jagatasya prāptaye,
  tasmād dhi śrutvā vimatiṃ vinodayed, iti.(5)
  evam aprameyaguṇavarṇā ānanda sukhāvatī lokadhātuḥ.
  tasya khalu punar ānanda bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasya
P42
daśasu dikṣv ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukāsameṣu
buddhakṣetreṣu gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā buddhā bhagavanto
nāmadheyaṃ parikīrtayante, varṇaṃ bhāṣante, yaśaḥ
prakāśayanti, guṇam udīrayanti. tat kasya hetoḥ. ye
kecit sattvās tasya 'mitābhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ
śṛṇvanti, śrutvā cāntaśa ekacittotpādam apy adhyāśayena
prasādasahagatam utpādayanti, sarve te 'vaivarttikatāyāṃ
saṃtiṣṭhante 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ.
  ye cānanda kecit sattvās taṃ tathāgataṃ punaḥ punar
ākārato manasīkariṣyanti, bahuparimitaṃ ca kuśalamūlam
avaropayiṣyanti, bodhāya cittaṃ pariṇāmya tatra ca lokadhātāv
upapattaye praṇidhāsyanti, teṣāṃ so 'mitābhas
tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite
'nekabhikṣugaṇaparivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ sthāsyati. tatas
te taṃ bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasannacittāḥ santi, tatraiva
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapadyate. ya ānandākāṃkṣata,
kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā, kim ity ahaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme
tam amitābhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyeyam iti, tenānuttarāyāṃ
samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādyādhyāśayapatitayā saṃtatyā
tasmin buddhakṣetre cittaṃ saṃpreṣyopapattaye kuśalamūlāni
ca pariṇāmayitavyāni.
  ye punas taṃ tathāgataṃ na bhūyo manasīkariṣyanti, na
ca bahuparimitaṃ kuśalamūlam abhīkṣṇam avaropayiṣyanti,
tatra ca buddhakṣetre cittaṃ saṃpreṣayiṣyanti, teṣāṃ
tādṛśenaiva so 'mitābhas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho
P43
varṇasaṃsthānārohapariṇāhena bhikṣusaṃghaparivāreṇa, tādṛśa
eva buddhanirmito maraṇakāle purataḥ sthāsyati, te tenaiva
tathagatadarśanaprasādālambanena samādhināpramuṣitayā
smṛtyā cyutās, tatraiva buddhakṣetre pratyājaniṣyanti.
  ye punar ānanda sattvās taṃ tathāgataṃ daśacittotpādāṃ
samanusmariṣyanti ; spṛhāṃś ca tasmin buddhakṣetre utpādayiṣyanti ;
gambhīreṣu ca dharmeṣu bhāṣyamāṇeṣu tuṣṭiṃ
pratilapsyante, na vipatsyante, na viṣādam āpatsyante, na
saṃsīdam āpatsyante ; 'ntaśa ekacittotpādenāpi taṃ tathāgataṃ
manasikariṣyanti, spṛhāṃ cotpādayiṣyanti tasmin buddhakṣetre,
te 'pi svapnāntaragatās tam amitābhaṃ tathāgataṃ drakṣyanti ;
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante ; 'vaivarttikāś
ca bhaviṣyanty anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ.
  imaṃ khalv ānandārthavasaṃ saṃpaśyantas, te tathāgatā
daśasu dikṣv aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāsu lokadhātusu tasyāmitābhasya
tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ parikīrtayanto, varṇān
ghoṣayantaḥ, praśaṃsām abhyudīrayanti. tasmin khalu
punar ānanda buddhakṣetre daśabhyo digbhya ekaikasyāṃ
diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā bodhisattvās tam amitābhaṃ
tathāgatam upasaṃkrāmanti darśanāya, vandanāya, paryupāsanāya,
paripraśnīkaraṇāya ; taṃ ca bodhisattvagaṇaṃ tāṃś
ca buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadaviśeṣān draṣṭum.
  atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyām imam evārthaṃ
bhūyasyā mātrayā paridīpayann imā gāthā abhāṣata :
P44
  yathaiva gaṅgāya nadīya vālikā,
  buddhāna kṣetrā purimena tāttakāḥ.
  yato hi te āgami buddha vanditum
  saṃbodhisattvā amitāyu nāyakaṃ.(1)
  bahupuṣpapuṭān gṛhītvā
  nānāvarṇa surabhī manoramān,
  okiranti naranāyakottamam
  amita-āyu naradevapūjitam.(2)
  tatha dakṣiṇapaścimottarāsu
  buddhāna kṣetrā diśatāsu tattakāḥ,
  yato yato āgami buddha vanditum
  saṃbodhisattvā amitāyu nāyakaṃ.(3)
  bahugandhapuṭān gṛhītvā
  nānāvarṇa surabhī manoramān,
  okiranti naranāyakottamaṃ
  amita-āyu naradevapūjitam.(4)
  pūjitva ca te bahubodhisattvān,
  vanditva pādām amitaprabhasya,
  pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vadanti caivaṃ :
  aho 'dbhutaṃ śobhati buddhakṣetraṃ.(5)
  te puṣpapuṭāhi samokiranti
  udagracittā atulāya prītaye,
  vācaṃ prabhāṣanti punas tu : nāyake,
  asmāpi kṣetraṃ siya evarūpaṃ.(6)
P45
  taiḥ puṣpapuṭā iti kṣipta tatra
  cchatraṃ tadā saṃsthihi yojanāśatāṃ,
  svalaṃkṛtaṃ śobhati citradaṇḍaṃ,
  cchādeti buddhasya samantakāyaṃ.(7)
  te bodhisattvās tatha satkaritvā,
  kathā kathentī iti tatra tuṣṭaḥ :
  sulabdha lābhāḥ khalu tehi sattvaiḥ,
  yehī śrutaṃ nāma narottamasya.(8)
  asmehi pī lābha sulabdha pūrvā
  yad āgatasya ima buddhakṣetraṃ.
  paśyātha svapnopama kṣetra kīdṛśaṃ,
  yat kalpitaṃ kalpasahasra śāstunā.(9)
  paśyatha, buddho varapuṇyarāśiḥ,
  parīvṛtu śobhati bodhisattvaiḥ.
  amitābhasya ābhā amitaṃ ca tejaḥ,
  amitā ca āyur, amitaś ca saṃghaḥ.(10)
  smitaṃ karontī amitāyu nāthaḥ
  ṣaṭtriṃśatkoṭīnayutāni arciṣāṃ,
  ye niścaritvā mukhamaṇḍalābhaḥ
  sphuranti kṣetrāṇi sahasrakoṭīḥ.(11)
  tāḥ sarva arcīḥ punaretya tatra,
  mūrdhne ca astaṃgami nāyakasya.
  devamanuṣyā janayanti prītim,
P46
  arcis tadā astam itā viditvā.(12)
  uttiṣṭhate buddhasuto mahāyaśā
  nāmnātha so hi avalokiteśvaraḥ :
  ko hetur atra bhagavan, ko pratyayaḥ,
  yena smitaṃ kurvasi lokanātha.(13)
  taṃ vyākarohī paramārthakovidā
  hitānukampī bahusattvamocakaḥ.
  śrutvā ti vācaṃ paramāṃ manoramāṃ,
  udagracittā bhaviṣyanti sattvāḥ.(14)
  ye bodhisattvā bahulokadhātuṣu
  sukhāvatīṃ prasthita buddhapaśyanā,
  te śrutva prītiṃ vipulāṃ janetvā,
  kṣipraṃ imaṃ kṣetra vilokayeyuḥ.(15)
  āgatya ca kṣetram idaṃ udāraṃ,
  ṛddhībalaṃ prāpuṇi kṣipram eva,
  divyaṃ ca cakṣus, tatha śrotra divyaṃ,
  jātismaraḥ paramatakovidāś ca.(16)
  amitāyu buddhas tada vyākaroti :
  mama hy ayaṃ praṇidhir abhūṣi pūrva.
  kathaṃ pi sattvāḥ śruṇiyāna nāmaṃ,
  vrajeyu kṣetraṃ mama nityam eva.(17)
  sa me aya praṇidhi prapūrṇa śobhanā,
  sattvāś ca enti bahulokadhātutaḥ.
  āgatya kṣipraṃ mama te 'ntikasmin
  avivarttikā bhontiha ekajātiyā.(18)
  tasmād ya icchatiha bodhisattvaḥ :
  mamāpi kṣetraṃ siya evarūpaṃ.
  ahaṃ pi sattvā bahu mocayeyaṃ,
P47
  nāmena ghoṣena tha darśanena.(19)
  sa śīghraśīghraṃ tvaramāṇarūpaḥ,
  sukhāvatīṃ gacchatu lokadhātuṃ.
  gatvā ca pūrvam amitaprabhasya,
  pūjetu buddhāna sahasrakoṭī.(20)
  buddhāna koṭīṃ bahu pūjayitvā,
  ṛddhībalena bahu kṣetra gatvā,
  kṛtvāna pūjāṃ sugatāna santike,
  bhaktāgram eṣyanti sukhāvatī ta, iti.(21)
  tasya khalu punar ānanda bhagavato 'mitāyuṣas tathāgatasyārhataḥ
samyaksaṃbuddhasya bodhivṛkṣaḥ ṣoḍasayojanaśatāny
uccaitvenāṣṭau yojanaśatāny abhipralambitaśākhāpattrapalāśaḥ
pañcayojanaśatamūlārohapariṇāhaḥ, sadāpattraḥ
sadāpuṣpaḥ sadāphalo, nānāvarṇo 'nekaśatasahasravarṇo,
nānāpattro nānāpuṣpo nānāphalo, nānāvicitrarūpena samalaṃkṛtaś,
candrabhāsamaṇiratnaparisphuṭaḥ, śakrābhilagnamaṇiratnavicitritaś,
cintāmaṇiratnakīrṇaḥ, sāgaravaramaṇiratnasuvicitrito,
divyasamatikrāntaḥ, suvarṇasūtrābhipralambito, rūcakahāro
ratnahāro vajrāhāraḥ kaṭakahāro lohitamuktāhāro
nīlamuktāhāraḥ, siṃhalatāmekhalākalāparatnasūtrasarva-
ratnakañcukaśatābhivicitritaḥ, suvarṇajālamuktājālasarvaratna-
jālakaṅkaṇījālāvanato, makarasvastikanandyāvartyardhacandra-
samalaṃkṛtaḥ, kiṅkiṇīmaṇisauvarṇasarvaratnālaṃkāravibhūṣito,
yathāśayasattvavijñaptisamalaṃkṛtaś ca.
  tasya khalu punar ānanda bodhivṛkṣasya vātasamīritasya
yaḥ śabdaghoṣo niścarati, so 'parimāṇān lokadhātūn abhivijñāpayati.
tatrānanda yeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhivṛkṣaśabdaḥ
P48
śrotrāvabhāsam āgacchati, teṣāṃ śrotrarogo na pratikāṃkṣitavyo,
yāvad bodhiparyantam. yeṣāṃ cāprameyāsaṃkhyeyā-
cintyāmāpyāparimāṇānabhilāpyānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhivṛkṣaś
cakṣuṣābhāsam āgacchati, teṣāṃ cakṣūrogo na pratikāṃkṣitavyo,
yāvad bodhiparyantam. ye khalu punar ānanda
sattvās tato bodhivṛkṣād gandhaṃ jighranti, teṣāṃ yāvad
bodhiparyantaṃ na jātu ghrāṇarogaḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyaḥ. ye
sattvās tato bodhivṛkṣāt phalāny āsvādayanti, teṣāṃ yāvad
bodhiparyantaṃ na jātu jihvārogaḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyaḥ.
ye sattvās tasya bodhivṛkṣasyābhayā sphuṭā bhavanti,
teṣāṃ yāvad bodhimaṇḍaparyantaṃ na jātu kāyarogaḥ
pratikāṃkṣitavyaḥ. ye khalu punar ānanda sattvās taṃ
bodhivṛkṣaṃ dharmato nidhyāyanti, teṣāṃ tatropādāya yāvad
bodhiparyantaṃ na jātu cittavikṣepaḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyaḥ. sarve
ca te sattvāḥ sahadarśanāt tasya bodhivṛkṣasyāvaivarttikāḥ
saṃtiṣṭhante ; yad utānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhes tisraś ca
kṣāntīḥ pratilabhante, yad idaṃ : ghoṣānugām anulomikāṃ
anutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ ca ; tasyaivāmitāyuṣas tathāgatasya
pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānena, pūrvajinakṛtādhikāratayā,
pūrvapraṇidhānaparicaryayoś ca susamāptayā, subhāvitayānū-
nāvikalatayā.
  tatra khalu punar ānanda ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ
pratyājāyante pratyājaniṣyante vā, sarve ta ekajātipratibaddhās
tata evānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante ;
sthāpayitvā praṇidhānavaśena ye te bodhisattvā mahāsiṃhanādanāditā,
P49
udārasaṃnāhasamnaddhāḥ, sarvasattvaparinirvāṇābhiyuktāś
ca.
  tasmin khalu punar ānanda buddhakṣetre ye śrāvakās
te vyomaprabhā, ye bodhisattvās te yojanakoṭīśatasahasraprabhāḥ ;
sthāpayitvā dvau bodhisattvau, yayoḥ prabhayā
sā lokadhātuḥ satatasamitaṃ nityāvabhāsasphuṭā.
  atha khalv āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat :
kiṃ nāmadheyau bhagavan tau satpuruṣau bodhisattvau
mahāsattvau. bhagavān āha : ekas tayor ānandāvalokiteśvara
bodhisattvo mahāsattvo, dvitīyaḥ sthāmaprāpto nāma. ita
evānanda buddhakṣetrāc cyutvā tatropapannau.
  tatra cānanda buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ,
sarve te dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ,
paripūrṇagātrā, dhyānābhijñākovidāḥ, prajñāprabhedakovidāḥ,
kuśalās, tīkṣṇendriyāḥ, susaṃvṛtendriyā, ājñātendriyā, adīnācalendriyāḥ,
pratilabdhakṣāntikā anantāparyantaguṇāḥ.
  tasmin khalu punar ānanda buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ
pratyājātāḥ, sarve te 'virahitā buddhadarśanena dharmaśravaṇenāvinipāta-
dharmāṇo, yāvad bodhiparyantaṃ. sarve ca
te tatropādāya na jātv ajātismarā bhaviṣyanti, sthāpayitvā
tathārūpeṣu kalpasaṃkṣobheṣu ye pūrvasthānapraṇihitāḥ
pañcasu kaṣāyeṣu vartamāneṣu, yadā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ
P50
loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, tad yathāpi nāma mamaitarhi.
  tasmin khalu punar ānanda buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ
pratyājātāḥ, sarve ta ekapurobhaktenānyalokadhātūṃ gatvānekani
buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇy upatiṣṭhanti, yāvac
cākāṃkṣanti buddhānubhāvena te yathā cittam utpādayanty :
evaṃrūpaiḥ puṣpadīpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇa-
cīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantītūryasaṃgītivādyaiḥ pūjāṃ
kuryāma iti, teṣāṃ sahacittotpādāt tathārūpāṇy eva sarvapūjāvidhānāni
pāṇau prādurbhavanti. te taiḥ puṣpair yāvad
vādyais teṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu pūjāṃ kurvanto bahvapa-
rimāṇāsaṃkhyeyaṃ kuśalamūlam upacinvanti. sacet punar
ākāṃkṣanty : evaṃrūpāḥ puṣpapuṭāḥ pāṇau prādurbhavanti,
teṣāṃ sahacittotpādān nānāvarṇā anekavarṇā nānāgandhā divyāḥ
puṣpapuṭāḥ pāṇau prādurbhavanti. te tais tathārūpaiḥ
puṣpapuṭaiḥ tān buddhān bhagavato 'vakiranti sma, abhyavakiranty,
abhiprakiranti. teṣāṃ ca yaḥ sarvaparīttaḥ puṣpapuṭa
utsṛṣṭo, daśayojanavistāram puṣpacchatraṃ prādurbhavanti.
upary antarīkṣe dvitīye cānutsṛṣṭe, na prathamo
dharaṇyāṃ prapatati. santi tatra puṣpapuṭā ya utsṛṣṭāḥ santo
viṃśatiyojanavistārāṇi puṣpacchatrāṇy upary antarīkṣe
prādurbhavanti. santi triṃśatcatvāriṃśatpañcāśat, santi yojana-
śatasahasravistārāṇi puṣpacchatrāṇy upary antarīkṣe prādurbhavanti.

body.translated_text: Moreover, from all four directions winds blow, which, as before, scatter fresh flowers. Just as in the morning, so too at midday, in the afternoon, at twilight, in the first watch of the night, in the middle and last watches. And those beings, being touched by those blowing winds perfumed with various fragrances, become endowed with such happiness, just like a monk who has attained the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation of perception and feeling). And in that Buddha-field, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is no designation or name whatsoever for fire, moon, sun, planets, constellations, stars, or for gloom and darkness. There is no designation whatsoever for night and day, except by way of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> conventional speech. And there is no notion whatsoever of household or possessions. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, at the proper time, clouds of divine fragrant water rain down. Divine flowers of all colors, divine seven jewels, divine sandalwood powder, and divine parasols, banners, and flags rain down. Divine palaces and divine canopies are held, divine jewel-parasols with chowries are held in the sky. Divine musical instruments are played. And divine <s>apsarases</s> dance. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that Buddha-field, those beings who have been born, are being born, or will be born, are all established in the right path, up to the point of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Because there, there is no establishment or designation of two groups, namely: those not destined, or those destined for wrong views. For this reason also, <s>Ānanda</s>, that world-realm is called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> in brief, but not in full. Even an <s>kalpa</s> (eon), <s>Ānanda</s>, would come to an end while enumerating the causes of happiness in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; but it is not possible to reach the limit of those causes of happiness. Then the Blessed One at that time spoke these verses: 'May all beings become <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones), with pure knowledge, skilled in the ultimate truth. Even if they were to proclaim the praise of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> for a <s>koṭi</s> of <s>kalpas</s> or even longer, (1) those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> would come to an end, but not the end of the praise of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. Their eloquence would not be exhausted while proclaiming the garland of its praise. (2) If one were to cut, break, and pulverize a world-realm into particles like atoms, and having filled many more world-realms beyond that with jewels, were to give them as a gift, (3) not even a fraction or a comparison of that merit would be the vast world-realms, compared to the merit that arises here from merely hearing the name of the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. (4) Much greater would be the merit of those who have faith in the perception of the <s>Jina's</s> word. For faith is the root for attaining the world; therefore, having heard, one should dispel doubt.' (5) Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s> is of immeasurable qualities and praise. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, in the ten directions, in each single direction, in Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, Blessed Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> proclaim his name, speak his praise, celebrate his fame, and extol his qualities. For what reason? Any beings who hear the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, and having heard it, generate even a single thought-moment accompanied by serene faith and noble intention, all of them become established in the state of non-regression from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, any beings who will repeatedly bring that <s>Tathāgata</s> to mind with his features, who will plant abundant roots of merit, who, dedicating their minds to enlightenment, will make a vow for rebirth in that world-realm, for them, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, will stand before them at the time of death, surrounded and honored by a great assembly of monks. Then, seeing that Blessed One, they have serene minds and are reborn in that very world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family, desires, 'How may I see that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> in this very life?', by that person, having generated the mind for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, with a continuous stream of noble intention, the mind should be directed toward that Buddha-field, and roots of merit should be dedicated for rebirth there. But for those who will not bring that <s>Tathāgata</s> repeatedly to mind, and will not frequently plant abundant roots of merit, but will direct their minds toward that Buddha-field, for them, a Buddha-manifestation just like that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, with the same complexion, form, height, and breadth, and with the same retinue of monks, will stand before them at the time of death. They, having passed away with unfailing mindfulness through the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that has as its object the serene faith from seeing that <s>Tathāgata</s>, will be reborn in that very Buddha-field. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, those beings who will recollect that <s>Tathāgata</s> for ten thought-moments, and will generate aspiration for that Buddha-field, and who, when the profound <s>Dharmas</s> are being taught, will obtain satisfaction, will not be distressed, will not fall into despair, will not become disheartened; who will bring that <s>Tathāgata</s> to mind with even a single thought-moment and will generate aspiration for that Buddha-field, they too, while in a dream, will see that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>; they will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; and they will become non-regressing from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Perceiving this very benefit, <s>Ānanda</s>, those <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions, in immeasurable and innumerable world-realms, proclaiming the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, announce his praises and extol his renown. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, to that Buddha-field, from the ten directions, from each single direction, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> approach that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> to see him, to pay homage to him, to attend upon him, and to question him; and to see that assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the particular perfections of the array of qualities and ornaments of that Buddha-field. Then the Blessed One at that time, illuminating this very meaning to a greater degree, spoke these verses: 'Just as there are sands in the river <s>Ganges</s>, so many are the Buddha-fields in the eastern direction. From there come the Buddhas and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> to pay homage to the leader <s>Amitāyus</s>. (1) Taking many handfuls of flowers, of various colors, fragrant, and delightful, they scatter them upon the supreme leader of men, <s>Amitāyus</s>, worshipped by men and gods. (2) Likewise, in the southern, western, and northern directions, there are so many Buddha-fields, from which come the Buddhas and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> to pay homage to the leader <s>Amitāyus</s>. (3) Taking many handfuls of incense, of various colors, fragrant, and delightful, they scatter them upon the supreme leader of men, <s>Amitāyus</s>, worshipped by men and gods. (4) Having honored the many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and having paid homage to the feet of <s>Amitaprabha</s>, they circumambulate him and say thus: "Oh, how wonderful! The Buddha-field shines!" (5) They scatter handfuls of flowers with uplifted minds and incomparable joy, and they speak these words again: "O leader, may our field also be of such a kind." (6) When those handfuls of flowers are thus thrown there, a parasol then forms, a hundred <s>yojanas</s> in size, well-adorned, with a variegated staff, it shines, and covers the entire body of the Buddha. (7) Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having thus honored him, pleased, speak this discourse there: "Great indeed is the gain for those beings by whom the name of the best of men has been heard." (8) "For us, too, a great gain was obtained before, in that we have come to this Buddha-field. See what a dream-like field this is, which was conceived for a thousand <s>kalpas</s> by the Teacher." (9) "See, the Buddha, a heap of excellent merit, shines, surrounded by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The light of <s>Amitābha</s> is immeasurable, and his splendor is immeasurable, his life is immeasurable, and his <s>Saṃgha</s> (community) is immeasurable." (10) The lord <s>Amitāyus</s> smiles, and thirty-six hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of rays, issuing forth from the orb of his face, illuminate a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of fields. (11) All those rays, returning there, set upon the head of the leader. Gods and humans generate joy, knowing that the rays have then set. (12) A son of the Buddha of great fame, named <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, rises and asks: "What is the reason here, O Blessed One, what is the cause, for which you smile, O lord of the world?" (13) "Explain this, O you who are skilled in the ultimate truth, compassionate for the welfare of others, liberator of many beings. Hearing your supreme and delightful words, beings will become uplifted in mind." (14) "Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in many world-realms who have set out for <s>Sukhāvatī</s> to see the Buddha, hearing this, will generate great joy and will quickly behold this field." (15) "And having come to this noble field, they will quickly obtain the power of supernatural abilities, the divine eye, and likewise the divine ear, memory of past lives, and skill in the highest doctrines." (16) The Buddha <s>Amitāyus</s> then explains: "This was my vow in the past: 'How may beings, having heard my name, come to my field forever?'" (17) "That beautiful vow of mine is now fulfilled, and beings come from many world-realms. Having quickly come into my presence, they become non-regressing here, bound to only one more birth." (18) "Therefore, whichever <s>Bodhisattva</s> here desires: 'May my field also be of such a kind; may I also liberate many beings by my name, by its proclamation, and by my sight,' (19) let him go very quickly, in haste, to the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. And having gone before <s>Amitaprabha</s>, let him honor a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of Buddhas. (20) Having honored many <s>koṭis</s> of Buddhas, having gone to many fields by the power of supernatural abilities, having made offerings in the presence of the <s>Sugatas</s>, they will come to the best of abodes, <s>Sukhāvatī</s>." (21) Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, is sixteen hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height, with overhanging branches, leaves, and foliage of eight hundred <s>yojanas</s>, and a circumference at the base of five hundred <s>yojanas</s>. It always has leaves, always has flowers, always has fruit; it is of various colors, of many hundreds of thousands of colors; it has various leaves, various flowers, various fruits; it is adorned with various wonderful forms, resplendent with moon-brilliant jewels, variegated with jewels attached by <s>Śakra</s>, strewn with wish-fulfilling jewels, beautifully variegated with the best ocean-jewels, transcending the divine. It is hung with golden threads, with necklaces of gold, necklaces of jewels, necklaces of diamonds, necklaces of bracelets, necklaces of red pearls, and necklaces of blue pearls; it is beautifully adorned with hundreds of jewel-bodices and threads of jewels like the <s>siṃhalatā</s> creeper, girdles, and ornaments; it is bowed down with nets of gold, nets of pearls, nets of all jewels, and nets of bangles; it is adorned with makaras, svastikas, nandyāvartas, and half-moons; it is decorated with ornaments of small bells, gems, gold, and all jewels, and is adorned according to the intentions of beings. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the sound and roar that issues from that Bodhi tree when it is stirred by the wind makes itself known throughout immeasurable world-realms. There, <s>Ānanda</s>, for those beings for whom the sound of the Bodhi tree comes within the range of their hearing, no disease of the ear is to be expected, up to the very seat of enlightenment. And for those immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, boundless, and inexpressible beings for whom the Bodhi tree comes within the range of their sight, no disease of the eye is to be expected, up to the very seat of enlightenment. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, for those beings who smell the fragrance from that Bodhi tree, no disease of the nose is ever to be expected, up to the very seat of enlightenment. For those beings who taste the fruits from that Bodhi tree, no disease of the tongue is ever to be expected, up to the very seat of enlightenment. For those beings who are touched by the light of that Bodhi tree, no disease of the body is ever to be expected, up to the very seat of enlightenment. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, for those beings who contemplate that Bodhi tree according to the <s>Dharma</s>, from that point on, no distraction of the mind is ever to be expected, up to the very seat of enlightenment. And all those beings, upon seeing that Bodhi tree, become established in the state of non-regression from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and they obtain three <s>kṣāntis</s> (acceptances), namely: the <s>ghoṣānugā</s> (acceptance following the sound), the <s>anulomikī</s> (acceptance in conformity with the truth), and the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena); by the power of the previous vow of that very <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, by their service rendered to past <s>Jinas</s>, and by the complete fulfillment, perfect cultivation, and flawless completeness of their previous vows and practices. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have been reborn there, are being reborn, or will be reborn, are all bound to only one more birth and from there will awaken to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; with the exception of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, by the power of their vow, have roared the great lion's roar, are clad in the noble armor, and are dedicated to the final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> of all beings. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that Buddha-field, the <s>Śrāvakas</s> have a light like the sky, and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have a light of a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yojanas</s>; with the exception of two <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by whose light that world-realm is constantly and perpetually pervaded with illumination. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'What are the names, O Blessed One, of those two great beings, those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'One of them, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>; the second is named <s>Sthāmaprāpta</s>. Having passed away from this very Buddha-field, <s>Ānanda</s>, they were reborn there.' And in that Buddha-field, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn are all endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person, with perfect bodies, skilled in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption) and the <s>abhijñās</s> (super-knowledges), skilled in the analysis of wisdom, virtuous, with sharp faculties, with well-restrained faculties, with faculties of perfect knowledge, with faculties that are not downcast or wavering, having obtained the <s>kṣāntis</s> (acceptances), and possessing infinite and boundless qualities. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that Buddha-field, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn are never separated from seeing the Buddha and hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and are not subject to falling back, up to the very seat of enlightenment. And all of them, from that point on, will never be without the memory of past lives, with the exception of those who, in such times of the decline of the <s>kalpa</s>, have made vows for a previous station, when the five corruptions are present, when Blessed Buddhas appear in the world, just as is the case with me now. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that Buddha-field, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn, in the time of a single morning meal, go to other world-realms and attend upon many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddhas. And as they wish, by the power of the Buddha, as they generate the thought, 'May we make offerings with such things as flowers, lamps, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, pennants, and musical instruments with song and music,' simultaneously with the arising of the thought, all such means of offering appear in their hands. Making offerings to those Blessed Buddhas with those flowers and so on, up to musical instruments, they accumulate many immeasurable and innumerable roots of merit. If, again, they wish, 'May such handfuls of flowers appear in our hands,' simultaneously with the arising of the thought, divine handfuls of flowers of various colors, of many colors, and of various fragrances appear in their hands. With such handfuls of flowers, they scatter them upon those Blessed Buddhas, they shower them, they strew them. And of these, the very smallest handful of flowers that is released appears as a flower-parasol ten <s>yojanas</s> in width. In the sky above, before a second is released, the first does not fall to the ground. There are handfuls of flowers there which, when released, appear as flower-parasols twenty <s>yojanas</s> in width in the sky above. There are those of thirty, forty, fifty, and there are those that appear as flower-parasols a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in width in the sky above. There, those who generate noble joy and delight, and obtain noble elation of mind, having planted many immeasurable and innumerable roots of merit, and having attended upon many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddhas in a single morning, are again established in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, through the sustaining power and protection of the previous vow of that very <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, and through the well-distinguished and cultivated perfection, fulfillment, and completeness of his previous vow. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that Buddha-field, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn all speak a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> connected with omniscience. And in that Buddha-field, beings have no notion of possession; while walking about and wandering through that entire Buddha-field, they generate neither attachment nor aversion. When they set out, they set out with indifference, not with attachment; and their mind is never thus. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, for the beings who are reborn, there is no notion of 'other', no notion of 'self', no notion of 'mine', no conflict, no dispute, no opposition, no unequal mind; they have equal minds, minds of benefit, minds of loving-kindness, gentle minds, affectionate minds, pliable minds, serene minds, stable minds, minds free from hindrances, unagitated minds, undisturbed minds, minds practicing the conduct of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), minds that have entered the wisdom which is the basis of mind. They are like the ocean in wisdom, like <s>Meru</s> in intelligence with their accumulation of many qualities, delighting in the recitation of the factors of enlightenment, dedicated to the recitation of the Buddha's teachings; they reflect with the physical eye, they produce the divine eye, they have reached the state of the eye of wisdom, they have gone to the farther shore with the eye of the <s>Dharma</s>; producing the eye of a Buddha, teaching, illuminating, and extensively proclaiming; producing unimpeded knowledge, dedicated to the sameness of the three realms, with tamed minds, with peaceful minds, endowed with the non-perception of all phenomena, skilled in the etymology of origination, endowed with the etymology of the <s>Dharma</s>, skilled in what is to be accepted and what is to be rejected, skilled in the grounds of right and wrong methods; they dwell indifferent to worldly talk, they find the essence in transcendent talk. They are skilled in the investigation of all phenomena, dwelling in the knowledge of the pacification of the nature of all phenomena, their sphere being non-perception, possessing nothing, without grasping, without thought, without exertion, well-liberated without grasping, without blemish, abiding in the boundless, abiding at the root in the <s>abhijñās</s> (super-knowledges), with unattached minds, not shrinking back, dedicated to the profound <s>Dharmas</s>, they do not sink down. They have risen up into the entrance of the Buddha's knowledge, which is difficult to comprehend; they have attained the path of the single vehicle; they are without doubt, have crossed over uncertainty, have knowledge that does not depend on another, and are without conceit; they are like <s>Sumeru</s>, risen up in knowledge; like the ocean, unshakable in intelligence; they surpass the light of the moon and sun in wisdom and with their pure, white, and auspicious minds; and in the preeminence of their qualities, with a brilliance and radiance like the color of molten gold. They are like the earth in their endurance of the good and bad of all beings; like water in their washing away and carrying off the defilement of all afflictions; like the king of fire in their burning up of the afflictions that are the fuel of all phenomena; like the wind in their non-attachment to all worlds; like space in their penetration of all phenomena and in their possessing nothing whatsoever. They are like the lotus in their being unstained by all worlds; like a great cloud of kālānusāri incense in their thundering of the <s>Dharma</s>; like a great rain in their showering of the water of the <s>Dharma</s>; like a bull in their overcoming of the great assembly; like a great <s>nāga</s> (great being) in their supremely well-tamed minds; like a thoroughbred steed in their being well-disciplined; like the lion, the king of beasts, in their fearless confidence in their prowess; like the nyagrodha, the king of trees, in their protection of all beings; like <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, in their being unshaken by all other doctrines; like the sky in their cultivation of immeasurable loving-kindness; like <s>Mahābrahmā</s> in their being preceded by mastery over all wholesome roots and phenomena; like a bird in their lack of accumulation; like <s>Garuḍa</s>, the king of birds, in their destruction of other doctrines; like the <s>udumbara</s> flower in the rarity and desirability of their appearance. Like a <s>nāga</s>, they are well-concentrated, undistracted, with upright faculties; skilled in discernment, abundant in the fragrance of patience; not envious, not desiring the prosperity of others. They are confident in discourses on the <s>Dharma</s>; insatiable in the investigation of the <s>Dharma</s>; like lapis lazuli in their morality; a mine of jewels in their learning; with pleasing voices, with the sound of the great drum of the <s>Dharma</s>; beating the great drum of the <s>Dharma</s>; blowing the great conch of the <s>Dharma</s>; raising the great banner of the <s>Dharma</s>; lighting the great torch of the <s>Dharma</s>. They are discerning with wisdom, undeluded, faultless, with all impurities pacified, pure, without the smell of defilement, not greedy, delighting in sharing, with open generosity, with outstretched hands, delighting in sharing gifts of both the <s>Dharma</s> and material things, not stingy in giving, unattached, with unafraid minds, dispassionate, wise, heroic, capable of bearing burdens, steadfast, modest, incomparable, unobstructed, having attained the <s>abhijñās</s> (super-knowledges), amiable, easy to live with, beneficial, illuminators of the world, leaders. Their craving, desire, flattery, and aversion are abandoned; they are pure, with sorrow gone, stainless, with the three defilements abandoned, delighting in the <s>abhijñās</s> (super-knowledges), powerful in causes, powerful in vows, not crooked, not deceitful. They are those who have planted roots of merit with many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddhas, who have uprooted the dart of pride, whose passion, hatred, and delusion have departed, who are pure, with pure conviction, praised by the best of <s>Jinas</s>, wise in the world, risen up from refined knowledge, praised by the <s>Jinas</s>, endowed with elation of mind, heroic, firm, unequaled, complete, incomparable, dustless, patient, noble, preeminent, modest, steadfast, mindful, intelligent, with good progress, armed with the weapon of wisdom, meritorious, brilliant, with all impurities and defilements abandoned, dedicated to the eternal <s>Dharmas</s>. Of such a kind, <s>Ānanda</s>, in brief, are the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> in that Buddha-field. But in full, if a <s>Tathāgata</s> were to describe them with a lifespan lasting for a hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, it would not be possible to reach the limit of the qualities of those great beings. Nor would the confidence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> be exhausted. For what reason? Because both of these, <s>Ānanda</s>, are inconceivable and incomparable, namely: the qualities of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the unexcelled wisdom and eloquence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text:
api cānanda uttiṣṭha paścānmukho bhūtvā, puṣpāṇy avakīryāñjaliṃ
pragṛhya, praṇipata. eṣāsau dig, yatra sa bhagavān
amitābhas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas tiṣṭhati dhriyate
P55
yāpayati, dharmaṃ ca deśayati ; virajo viśuddho, yasya
taṃ nāmadheyam anāvaraṇaṃ daśadiśi loke vighuṣṭam ekaikasyāṃ
diśi gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā buddhā bhagavanto varṇayanti,
stuvanti, praśaṃsanty, asakṛd asakṛd asaṅgavācāprativākyāḥ.
evam ukta, āyusmān ānando bhagavantam
etad avocat : icchāmy ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tam amitābham
amitaprabham amitāyuṣaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ
draṣṭum, tāṃś ca bodhisattvān mahāsattvān
bahubuddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlān. samanantarābhāṣitā
cāyuṣmatānandeneyaṃ vāk, atha tāvad eva
so 'mitābhas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ svapāṇitalāt
tathārūpāṃ prabhāṃ prāmuñcat, yayedaṃ koṭīśatasahasratamaṃ
buddhakṣetraṃ mahatāvabhāsena sphuṭam abhūt.
  tena khalv api samayena sarvatra koṭīśatasahasrabuddhakṣetrāṇāṃ,
ye kecit kālaparvatā vā, ratnaparvatā vā,
merumahāmerumucilindamahāmucilindacakravāḍamahācakravāḍā
vā, bhittayo vā, stambhā vā, vṛkṣagahanodyānavimānāni
vā divyamānuṣyakāni, tāni sarvāṇi tasya tathāgatasya tayā
prabhayābhinirbhinnāny abhūvan, samabhibhūtāni.
  tad yathāpi nāma puruṣo vyāmamātrake sthito dvitīyaṃ
puruṣaṃ pratyavekṣata āditye 'bhyudgata ; evam evāsmin
buddhakṣetre bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā devanāgayakṣa-
gandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāś ca tasyāṃ velāyām
adrākṣus tam amitābhaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ,
sumerum iva parvatarājānaṃ sarvakṣetrābhyudgatam,
sarvadiso 'bhibhūya, bhāsamānaṃ tapantaṃ virocamānaṃ
P56
bibhrājamānaṃ, taṃ ca mahāntaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ, taṃ ca
bhikṣusaṃghaṃ, yad idaṃ buddhānubhāvena tasyāḥ prabhayāḥ
pariśuddhatvāt.
  tad yatheyaṃ mahāpṛthivy ekodakajātā bhavet, tatra na
vṛkṣā, na parvatā, na dvīpā, na tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayo,
na nadīśvabhraprapātāḥ prajñāyeran, anyatraikārṇavībhūtamahāpṛthivy
aikā syāt ; evam eva tasmin buddhakṣetre nāsty
anyat kiṃcil liṅgaṃ vā, nimittaṃ vānyatraiva vyāmaprabhāḥ
śrāvakās, te ca yojanakoṭīśatasahasraprabhā bodhisattvāḥ, sa
ca bhagavān amitābhas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas,
taṃ ca śrāvakagaṇaṃ taṃ ca bodhisattvagaṇam abhibhūya,
sarvā diśaḥ prabhāsayan saṃdṛśyate.
  tena khalv api samayena tasyāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau
bodhisattvāḥ śrāvākadevamanuṣyāś ca sarve ta imāṃ lokadhātuṃ,
śākyamuniṃ ca tathāgataṃ mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena
parivṛtaṃ paśyanti sma, dharmaṃ ca deśayantam.
  tatra khalu bhagavān ajitaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam
āmantrayate sma : paśyasi tvam ajitāmuṣmin buddhakṣetre
guṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadam ; upariṣṭāś cāntarīkṣa ārāmaramaṇīyāni,
vanaramaṇīyāny, udyānaramaṇīyāni, nadīpuṣkiriṇīramaṇīyāni,
nānāratnamayotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍaṛīkākīrṇāni ;
adhastāc ca dharaṇitalam upādāya, yāvad akaniṣṭhabhavanād,
gaganatalaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇaṃ, puṣpāvalisamupaśobhitaṃ,
nānāstambhapaṅktiparisphuṭaṃ tathāgatābhinirmita-
nānādvijasaṃghaniṣevitam. āha : paśyāmi bhagavan, bhagavān
āha : paśyasi punas tvam ajitaitān aparān dvijasaṃghān
P57
sarvabuddhakṣetrān buddasvareṇābhijijñāpayanti, yenaite
bodhisattvā nityam avirahitā buddhānusmṛtyā. āha : paśyāmi
bhagavan. bhagavān āha : paśyasi tvam ajitātra buddhakṣetre
amūn sattvān yojanaśatasahasrakeṣu vimāneṣv abhirūḍhān,
antarīkṣe 'saktān krāmataḥ. āha : paśyāmi bhagavan.
bhagavān āha : tat kiṃ manyase 'jita ; asti kiṃcin
nānātvaṃ devānāṃ vā paranirmitavaśavartināṃ sukhāvatyām
lokadhātau manuṣyaṇāṃ vā. āha : ekam apy ahaṃ bhagavan
nānātvaṃ na samanupaśyāmi. yāvad maharddhikā atra
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau manuṣyāḥ. bhagavān āha : paśyasi
punas tvam ajita tatra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv ekeṣāṃ
manuṣyāṇām udāreṣu padmeṣu garbhāvāsam. āha ; tad yathāpi
nāma bhagavan trayaśtriṃśā devā yāmā devā vā, pañcāśadyojanakeṣu
vā, yojanaśatikeṣu vā, pañcayojanaśatikeṣu
vimāneṣu praviṣṭāḥ krīḍanti, ramanti, paricārayanti ; evam
evāhaṃ bhagavan atra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv ekeṣāṃ
manuṣyāṇām udārapadmeṣu garbhāvāsaṃ paśyāmi.
  santi khalu punar atra bhagavan sattvā ya upapādukāḥ
padmeṣu paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti. tat ko 'tra bhagavan
hetuḥ, kaḥ pratyayo, yad anye punar garbhāvāse prativasanti ;
anye punar upapādukāḥ paryaṅkaiḥ padmeṣu prādurbhavanti.
bhagavān āha : ye te 'jita bodhisattvā anyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu
sthitāḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapattaye vicikitsām
P58
utpādayanti, tena cittena kuśalamūlāny avaropayanti,
teṣām atra garbhāvāso bhavati. ye punar nirvicikitsāś cchinnakāṃkṣāḥ
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapattaye kuśalamūlāny
avaropayanti, buddhānāṃ bhagavatām asaṅgajñānam avakalpayanty
abhiśraddhadhaty adhimucyante ; tatropapādukāḥ
padmeṣu paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti. ye te 'jita bodhisattvā
mahāsattvā anyatrabuddhakṣetrasthāś cittam utpādayanty
amitābhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya darśanāya,
na vicikitsām utpādayanti, na kāṃkṣanty asaṅgabuddhajñānaṃ,
svakucalamūlaṃ cābhiśraddhadhati, teṣām
aupapādukānāṃ paryaṅkaiḥ padmeṣu prādurbhūtānāṃ
muhūrtamātreṇaivaivaṃrūpaḥ kāyo bhavati, tad yathānyeṣāṃ
ciropapannānāṃ sattvānām.
  paśyājita prajñādaurbalyaṃ prajñāvaimātraṃ prajñāparihāṇiṃ
prajñāparīttatāṃ, yatra hi nāma pañcavarṣaśatāni parihīṇā
bhavanti buddhadarśanād, bodhisattvadarśanāt, saddharmadarśanād,
dhārmasaṃkathyāt ; kuśalamūlacaryāyāḥ parihīṇā
bhavanti sarvakuśalamūlasaṃpatter, yad idaṃ vicikitsāpatitaiḥ
saṃjñāmanasikāraiḥ.
  tad yathājita rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhānābhiṣiktasya
bandhanāgāraṃ bhavet, sarvasauvarṇavaiḍūryapratyuptam,
avasaktapaṭṭamālyadāmakalāpaṃ, nānāraṅgavitatavitānaṃ,
dūṣyapaṭṭasaṃcchannaṃ, nānāmuktakusumābhikīrṇam, udāraṃ,
dhūpanirdhūpitaṃ, prāsādaharmyagavākṣavedikātoraṇavicitra-
sarvaratnapratimaṇḍitaṃ, hemaratnakaṃkaṇījālasaṃcchannaṃ,
caturasraṃ, catuḥsthūṇaṃ caturdvāraṃ, catuḥsopānakam.
tatra tasya rājñaḥ putraḥ kenacid eva kṛtyena prakṣipto
P59
jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayair nigaḍair baddho bhavati. tasya
ca tatra paryaṅkaḥ prajñaptaḥ syād, anekagoṇikāstīrṇas,
tūlikāpalālikāstīrṇaḥ, kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśaḥ, kāliṅga-
prāvaraṇasottarapaṭacchadana, ubhayāntalohitopadhānaś, citro,
darśanīyaḥ. sa tatrābhiniṣaṇṇo vābhinipanno vā bhavet. bahu
cāsyānekavidhaṃ śucipraṇītaṃ pānabhojanaṃ tatropanāmyet.
tat kiṃ manyase 'jita ; udāras tasya rājaputrasya sa paribhogo
bhavet. āha : udāro bhagavan. bhagavān āha : tat kiṃ
manyase 'jita ; api tv āsvādayet, sa tan nigamayed vā,
tena vā tuṣṭiṃ vidyāt. āha : no hīdaṃ bhagavan. api tu
khalu punar yena vyapanītena rājñā tatra bandhanāgāre
prakṣipto bhavet, sa tato mokṣam evākāṃkṣayet. abhijātān
kumārān amātyān stryāgārān śreṣṭhino gṛhapatīn koṭṭarājño
vā paryeṣed, ya enaṃ tato bandhanāgārāt parimocayeyuḥ.
kiṃ cāpi bhagavaṃs tasya kumārasya tatra bandhanāgāre
nābhiratiḥ. nātra parimucyate, yāvan na rājā prasādam upadarśayati.
bhagavān āha : evam evājita, ye te bodhisattvāḥ
vicikitsāpatitāḥ kuśalamūlāny avaropayanti, kāṃkṣanti
buddhajñānam asamasamajñānaṃ, kiṃ cāpi te buddhanāmaśravaṇena,
tena ca cittaprasādamātreṇātra sukhāvatyāṃ
lokadhātāv upapadyante. na tu khalv aupapādukāḥ padmeṣu
paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti. api tu padmeṣu garbhāvāse
P60
prativasanti. kiṃ cāpi teṣāṃ tatrodyānavimānasaṃjñāḥ
saṃtiṣṭhante. nāsty uccāraprasrāvaṃ, nāsti kheṭasiṃhānakaṃ,
na pratikūlaṃ manasaḥ pravartate. api tu khalu punaḥ
pañca varṣaśatāni virahitā bhavanti buddhadarśanena,
dharmaśravaṇena, bodhisattvadarśanena, dharmasāṃkathyaviniścayena,
sarvakuśaladharmacaryābhiś ca. kiṃ cāpi te
tatra nābhiramante, na tuṣṭiṃ vidanti. api tu khalu punaḥ
pūrvāparādhaṃ kṣapayitvā, te bhūyas tataḥ paścān niṣkrāmanti.
na caiṣāṃ tato niṣkrāmatāṃ niṣkramaḥ prajñāyata, ūrdhvam
adhas tiryag vā.
  paśyājita ; yatra hi nāma pañcabhir varṣaśatair bahūni
buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇy upasthātavyāni, bahvasaṃkhyeyāprameyāni
ca kuśalamūlāny avaropayitavyāni ca syuḥ.
buddhadharmāś ca parigṛhītavyāḥ. tat sarvaṃ vicikitsādoṣeṇa
virāgayanti. paśyājita kiyan mahate 'narthāya
bodhisattvānāṃ vicikitsā saṃvartata iti.
  tasmāt tarhy ajita ; bodhisattvair nirvicikitsair bodhāya
cittam utpādya, kṣipraṃ sarvasattvahitasukhādhānāya
sāmarthāpratilambhārthaṃ, sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv
upapattaye kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayitavyāni, yatra bhagavān
amitāyus tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ.
  evam ukte, 'jito bodhisattvo bhagavantam etad avocat :
kiyantaḥ punar bhagavan bodhisattvā ito buddhakṣetrāt
pariniṣpannā, anyeṣāṃ vā buddhānāṃ bhagavatām antikād
ye sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante. bhagavān āha :
P61
ito hy ajita buddhakṣetrād dvāsaptatikoṭīnayutāni bodhisattvānāṃ
pariniṣpannāni, yāni sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante,
pariniṣpannānām avaivarttikānāṃ bahubuddhakoṭī-
śatasahasrāvaropitaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ. kaḥ punar vādas, tataḥ
parīttataraiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ.
  duṣprasahasya tathāgatasyāntikād aṣṭādaśakoṭīnayutāni
bodhisattvānāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante ;
  pūrvāntare digbhāge ratnākaro nāma tathāgato viharati.
tasyāntikān navatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyām lokadhātāv
upapatsyante ;
  jyotiṣprabhasya tathāgatasyāntikād dvāviṃśatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante ;
  amitaprabhasya tathāgatasyāntikāt pañcaviṃśatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante ;
  lokapradīpasya tathāgatasyāntikāt ṣaṣṭibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante ;
  nāgābhibhuvas tathāgatasyāntikāt catuḥṣaṣtibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ
sukhāvatyām lokadhātāv upapatsyante ;
  virajaprabhasya tathāgatasyāntikāt pañcaviṃśatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante ;
  siṃhasya tathāgatasyāntikād aṣṭādaśabodhisattvasahasrāṇi
sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyante ;
