body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, arise, turn to face the west, scatter flowers, join your palms, and prostrate. This is that direction where the Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, exists, lives, maintains himself, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>; he who is spotless and pure, whose unimpeded name is proclaimed in the world in the ten directions, in each single direction, Blessed Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> praise, extol, and celebrate him, again and again, with unimpeded speech and response." When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "I wish, O Blessed One, to see that <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Amitaprabha</s>, <s>Amitāyus</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, and those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> who have planted roots of merit with many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddhas." No sooner had the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> spoken this word, than that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, from the palm of his hand, released such a light that this hundred-thousandth <s>koṭi</s> of a Buddha-field was filled with a great radiance. And at that very moment, in all the hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of Buddha-fields, whatever black mountains, or jewel mountains, or <s>Merus</s>, <s>Mahāmerus</s>, <s>Mucilindas</s>, <s>Mahāmucilindas</s>, <s>Cakravāḍas</s>, or <s>Mahācakravāḍas</s>, or walls, or pillars, or groves, gardens, and palaces, whether divine or human, all of them were penetrated by that light of that <s>Tathāgata</s> and were surpassed. Just as a person standing at a fathom's distance might look at another person when the sun has risen; in the very same way, in this Buddha-field, the monks, nuns, male lay followers, female lay followers, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> at that time saw that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, like <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, risen above all fields, surpassing all directions, shining, blazing, glowing, resplendent, and that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and that assembly of monks; this being by the power of the Buddha and the purity of that light. Just as if this great earth were to become a single mass of water, where no trees, no mountains, no islands, no grasses, shrubs, herbs, or forests, no rivers, chasms, or precipices would be perceived, but only a single great earth that had become one ocean; in the very same way, in that Buddha-field, there was no other sign or mark whatsoever, except for the <s>Śrāvakas</s> with a light of a fathom, and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with a light of a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yojanas</s>, and that Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, who, surpassing that assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and that assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, was seen illuminating all directions. And at that very moment, in that world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, gods, and humans all saw this world-realm, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> surrounded by a great assembly of monks, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Ajita</s>: "Do you see, <s>Ajita</s>, the perfection of the array of qualities and ornaments in that Buddha-field; and above in the sky, the delightful groves, delightful forests, delightful gardens, delightful rivers and pools, filled with various jewel-lotuses, blue lotuses, water lilies, and white lotuses; and below, from the surface of the earth up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven, the sky is strewn with flowers, beautifully adorned with garlands of flowers, made distinct with rows of various pillars, and frequented by flocks of various birds created by the manifestation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?" He said: "I see, O Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "Do you see again, <s>Ajita</s>, these other flocks of birds making all the Buddha-fields known with the Buddha's voice, by which these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are never separated from the recollection of the Buddha?" He said: "I see, O Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "Do you see, <s>Ajita</s>, in this Buddha-field, those beings mounted in palaces a hundred thousand  unattached, traversing the sky?" He said: "I see, O Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Ajita</s>; is there any difference between the gods of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> heaven and the humans in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>?" He said: "I do not perceive even a single difference, O Blessed One. So great is the supernatural power of the humans here in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>." The Blessed One said: "Do you see again, <s>Ajita</s>, in that world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, the womb-dwelling of some humans in magnificent lotuses?" He said: "Just as, O Blessed One, the Thirty-three gods or the <s>Yāma</s> gods, having entered palaces of fifty <s>yojanas</s>, or a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, or five hundred <s>yojanas</s>, play, delight, and enjoy themselves; in the very same way, O Blessed One, I see the womb-dwelling of some humans in magnificent lotuses in this world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. But there are, O Blessed One, beings here who appear spontaneously on lotus thrones. What is the reason here, O Blessed One, what is the cause, that some again dwell in a womb-gestation, while others again appear spontaneously on lotus thrones?" The Blessed One said: "Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, who, being in other Buddha-fields, produce doubt about being born in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, and with that mind plant roots of merit, for them there is a womb-gestation here. But those who, without doubt and with their perplexity cut off, plant roots of merit for birth in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, and who comprehend, have faith in, and are convinced of the unimpeded knowledge of the Blessed Buddhas; they appear spontaneously on lotus thrones. Those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, who, being in other Buddha-fields, generate the mind to see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, and do not produce doubt, do not have perplexity about the unimpeded Buddha-knowledge, and have faith in their own roots of merit; for them, who have appeared spontaneously on lotus thrones, in a single moment a body of such a kind comes into being, just like that of other beings who have been born long ago. See, <s>Ajita</s>, the weakness of wisdom, the disparity of wisdom, the decline of wisdom, the smallness of wisdom, whereby for five hundred years they are deprived of seeing the Buddha, seeing the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, seeing the true <s>Dharma</s>, and of discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>; they are deprived of the practice of the roots of merit, of the perfection of all roots of merit; this being due to perceptions and mental applications that have fallen into doubt. Just as, <s>Ajita</s>, there might be a prison of a <s>kṣatriya</s> king, anointed on the head, inlaid with pure gold and lapis lazuli, with hanging cloth-garlands and festoons, with canopies of various colors spread out, covered with fine cloth, strewn with various fresh flowers, magnificent, fumigated with incense, beautifully adorned with palaces, upper stories, latticed windows, platforms, and gateways, decorated with all kinds of jewels, covered with nets of golden and jeweled bangles, square, with four pillars, four doors, and four staircases. There, a son of that king, having been cast in for some deed, is bound with fetters made of <s>Jambūnada</s> gold. And there for him a couch would be prepared, spread with many woolen blankets, spread with cotton and silk cushions, with the pleasant touch of <s>kācilindika</s> cloth, with a coverlet of <s>Kāliṅga</s> fabric, with red pillows at both ends, variegated, and beautiful to behold. He might be sitting or lying there. And much varied, pure, and excellent food and drink would be brought to him there. What do you think, <s>Ajita</s>; would that enjoyment of the prince be magnificent?" He said: "Magnificent, O Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Ajita</s>; would he savor it, would he enjoy it, or would he find satisfaction in it?" He said: "Indeed not, O Blessed One. Rather, by whichever king he was banished and cast into that prison, he would desire only liberation from it. He would seek out noble princes, ministers, the women of the court, merchants, householders, or provincial kings who might free him from that prison. And yet, O Blessed One, that prince has no delight in that prison. He is not freed from it until the king shows his favor." The Blessed One said: "In the very same way, <s>Ajita</s>, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, having fallen into doubt, plant roots of merit and are perplexed about the Buddha-knowledge, the knowledge that is unequal and equal; although by hearing the Buddha's name and by that mere serenity of mind they are reborn in this world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, they do not, however, appear spontaneously on lotus thrones. Rather, they dwell in a womb-gestation in lotuses. Although for them there, perceptions of gardens and palaces arise, there is no excretion or urination, no phlegm or mucus, nothing disagreeable to the mind occurs. But for five hundred years they are deprived of seeing the Buddha, of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, of seeing the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, of the analysis of discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, and of the practice of all wholesome qualities. Although they do not delight there, they do not find satisfaction. But, having exhausted their previous fault, they afterwards emerge from there. And for them, as they emerge from there, no exit is perceived, whether upwards, downwards, or sideways. See, <s>Ajita</s>; where in five hundred years many hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of Buddhas should have been attended upon, and many innumerable and immeasurable roots of merit should have been planted, and the qualities of a Buddha should have been taken up, all this they lose through the fault of doubt. See, <s>Ajita</s>, how great a misfortune doubt becomes for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having generated the mind for enlightenment without doubt, in order to quickly attain the capacity for establishing the welfare and happiness of all beings, should dedicate their roots of merit for birth in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, where the Blessed One <s>Amitāyus</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, resides. When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ajita</s> said this to the Blessed One: "But how many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, O Blessed One, who have set out from this Buddha-field, or from the presence of other Blessed Buddhas, will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>?" The Blessed One said: "From this Buddha-field, <s>Ajita</s>, seventy-two <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have set out, who will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, having set out as non-regressing ones, with roots of merit planted with many hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of Buddhas. What then is to be said of those with fewer roots of merit? From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Duṣprasaha</s>, eighteen <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; In the eastern quarter, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnākara</s> dwells. From his presence, ninety <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotiṣprabha</s>, twenty-two <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitaprabha</s>, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokapradīpa</s>, sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Nāgābhibhū</s>, sixty-four <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Virajaprabha</s>, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siṃha</s>, eighteen thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>; From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śrīkūṭa</s>, eighty-one <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be reborn in the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>;
